[/list]

notes.title: BIOLUM OFFICIAL RELEASE DATE: DECEMBER 2nd
notes.content:
[b]Hello Biolum enthusiasts,[/b] are you as excited as we are for the release? It is just around the corner and we can't wait to share our experience with you.

The [b]Biolum[/b] world plunges us into the depths of the deep ocean. Ordinarily pitch black, the Biolum universe is glowing with light and life. And so to get an idea of what this universe is like, we are sharing with you a part of this undersea adventure.

[h3]Click below for a pre-release sneak peak![/h3]
https://sketchfab.com/models/0f47d322bd69488bb2a10ce0aed5fddc/embed [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36096800/e3fca853e02ba37ffb5adcf6b2e62420fd3cfdbf.jpg[/img] [i]If Sketchfab does not load, please use this link:[url=https://sketchfab.com/models/0f47d322bd69488bb2a10ce0aed5fddc/embed]The World of BIOLUM[/url][/i]

Explore and share with your friends. Dive into the cosmic unknown, you never know what you'll find…

[h3]And of course, we will be here next week on [b]December 2nd at 9:00am PST for the official release![/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36096800/c953a6c03973be5a123b61f3b184f1a1412f04e0.gif[/img]

[*] fixed an issue in Sc1-3 where the Harness have had an unintentional offset
[*] fixed an issue, where the player gets abruptly rotated in Sc12 when getting dragged by the glimmung
[*] fixed an issue with the fish swarms, where they could swim through geometry unhindered in several Scenes
[*] fixed an issue, where a sound of Rachael in Sc9 seemed unintentionally cut-off
[*] fixed an issue, where the fade to black at the end of Sc14 was broken

[list]

[/list]

notes.title: Biolum VR Beta 0.6 is there!
notes.content:
[h1]Biolum VR (0.6.3220.0fa6499) Release Notes[/h1]
In this Update we concentrated mostly on increasing performance. In the last build we saw huge hiccups and were having big frame drops throughout the experience. For the long term we needed to swap to a higher Engine Version as well. With that, we can better answer technical issues to come.


[h2]Known Issues[/h2]
[list]
[*] currently iterating on the best lightmap solutions, there might still be some issues
[*] currently adjusting timings and interaction in Sc6 Puzzle and Sc8 Puzzle, yet using a fallback version of both in this build
[*] we are aware of fish swarms sometimes swimming through geometry (Sc3, Sc8, Sc10)
[*] we are aware that the player get abruptly rotated (by 20°) in Sc12, while getting dragged by the Glimmung
[/list]

[h2]Added[/h2]
[list]
[*] with the swap to a newer engine, we are now using a newer input system, which allows us to respond better to different VR devices - so we upgraded to OpenXR, as OpenVR will be deprecated by VR runtimes like Oculus, SteamVR etc.
[*] we are now using Screen Spaced Ambient Occlusion (SSAO) as a post effect
[*] we added a new system to reduce the Vertex Count of assets within their lowest LoDs, saving up performance
[/list]

[h2]Changed[/h2]
[list]
[*] General: Upgraded to a newer Engine Version (from Unity 2019.4 to Unity 2020.3)
[*] General: Updated various external and internal packages to provide better long term service
[*] General: switched from the web-Gitlab to our inhouse Git, to provide better controllability
[*] Assets: Chrysaora jellyfish is now way more performant (shaderbased)
[*] Environment: each scene was filled with lots of chunk over the past development years. We cleaned that up, saving lots of vertices and objects, without changing the  experience visually. Also increasing our flexibility to work on issues.
[*] Environment: adjusted the vertex distribution in each scene. That means, we are trying to achieve a well balanced scene, where small objects have a low amount of vertices and big objects have a higher amount.
[*] Vegetation: Slightly increased the count in Scenes 4, 5, 6, 7
[*] Vegetation: Slightly reduced the count in Scenes 12 and 14 as it was necessary to provide performance
[/list]

[h2]Fixed[/h2]
[list]
[*] fixed every broken Scatter throughout the experience
[*] fixed an issue, when the Torchlight was rendered behind certain objects
[/list]

[h2]Removed[/h2]
[list]
[*] removed a feature, that was causing render issues (Tearing) in VR
[*] fully disabled reflection probes for now, as they were causing lots of lightmaps issues; can be reimplemented when everything else is fixed
[*] fully disabled the Biolum Control feature, as it was deprecated and nowhere (throughout the experience) used any longer
[*] fully disabled any island-based realtime custom lights, as they were pretty performance expensive and we were not using them with their initial use-case. Almost all custom lights are now used as bakelights, except for a few hero animations.
[*] fully disabled the GlimCall ShaderSubmodule as it was never used any longer and slowing down the experience
[/list]

notes.title: Weekly Update #3
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36096800/d64d1f67ce5c54f5f2edf23945ea63873099bfb1.gif[/img]

This update encompasses first versions of [b]all four prototype levels[/b]. They can be selected from the Grip Menu. 2,3, and 4 are "waypoints" inside the large cave, 1 is a separate scene for now.

[b]Prototype Level 1[/b] is included as a separate scene (use the grip button to open the menu and select the leftmost option - Level 1/Rattail Fish - to load the level 1 scene).

For[b] Prototype level 2[/b] we have iterations on the HUD and warnings graphics, spline path, helmet behaviour and interior as well as a first versions of environment scanning.

For [b]Prototype level 3[/b] we have the ability to swim through all the caves using the Soft Rail technique.

For [b]Prototype level 4[/b] we have a procedurally animated close-encounter of our huge creature.

[b]You can switch between the scenes using the keyboard[/b] by either pressing 1 (Cave Interaction Prototype Scene) or 2 (Rattail Scene) [b]or via the menu by pressing the Grip Button[/b] on your VR controller and selecting the menu item.

notes.title: Initial Prototype #1
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36096800/62fbcb4f371bbf336d803db5092664c9dc59bee3.gif[/img]

The first Prototype Release includes a couple of basic movement types, which use the Trigger Buttons on your controllers:
[list]
[*] (1) Rail
[*] (2) Modified Rail (Soft Rail)
[*] (3) Waypoints 
[*] (4) Freedom (Free Roam) 
[*] (5) Swimming
[*] (6) Climbing
[*] (7) Grab Navigation
[/list]
By pressing both the Grip Buttons on your Left Controller a Menu appears in front of you to select either a Movement Type or teleport to a specific location in the greybox level  - have fun!
